de35_texts.topic: The texts on rule, rights and the unproductive: Land's e-book, the NYT interview, the 2021 universities line, the New Yorker summary

claims.text: Land p.5, quoting Moldbug: a state is 'a business which owns a country'; 'Each share has one vote, and the shareholders elect a board, which hires and fires managers'; 'This business's customers are its residents'

Land p.6 (his own gloss): once shares exist 'the owners of the state can initiate rational corporate governance, beginning with the appointment of a CEO'; 'There is no longer any need for residents (clients) to take any interest in politics whatsoever. In fact, to do so would be to exhibit semi-criminal proclivities'; taxes are 'sovereign rent'; residents 'can notify its customer service function'; 'No voice, free exit'

Land p.6, quoting Moldbug: Hong Kong, Singapore and Dubai have 'minimal crime and high levels of personal and economic freedom'; 'They are weak only in political freedom, and political freedom is unimportant by definition when government is stable and effective'

Land p.5: Moldbug's recognition that 'sovereignty cannot be eliminated, caged, or controlled' and 'constitutions have exactly as much real authority as a sovereign interpretative power allows them to have'
Land p.10 quotes Steve Hanke approvingly: 'The only thing that the citizens can demand from the State, under the Bill of Rights, is for a trial by a jury'

Land p.18: social disadvantage 'in large part - perhaps overwhelmingly large part - ... reflects sheer misfortune'; 'Dim, impulsive, unhealthy, and unattractive people, reared chaotically in abusive families ... have every reason to curse the gods before themselves'; 'In regards to effective incentive structures, however, none of this is of the slightest importance'; 'Whatever is subsidized is promoted'
Land p.25: 'The war on poverty creates a chronically dysfunctional underclass'

NYT 18 Jan 2025: asked about Nero and twentieth-century dictators, Yarvin said 'Your question is the most important question of all' and gave no mechanism for removing a bad ruler; on CEOs: 'if you took any of the Fortune 500 CEOs, some of them are good ... Some of them are bad, but the overall quality, you know, just pick one at random and put him or her in charge of Washington'

NYT 18 Jan 2025: 'So free speech is a freedom. The right to vote is a form of power'; 'voting is providing this almost pornographic stimulus'; the New York Times is 'a fifth generation hereditary absolute monarchy'; government workers should be seen as 'a normal person serving a regime' that did strange things

Harvard Crimson (6 May 2025): in a 2021 Substack post Yarvin wrote that 'regime change' would require that 'all accredited universities be both physically and economically liquidated'; at the 5 May 2025 debate he said Harvard should be remade, not destroyed

The New Yorker (9 June 2025) summarised Moldbug's proposed regime: it 'would sell off public schools, destroy universities, abolish the press, and imprison "decivilized populations"'; also quoted a call for 'the liquidation of democracy, the Constitution, and the rule of law'
